text: Are there any E. coli expression studies about ciprofloxacin?

Below is a summary study report formulated after querying GEO for E. coli expression datasets that include ciprofloxacin in their descriptions.

------------------------------------------------------------------
Abstract

We investigated whether publicly deposited expression studies in Escherichia coli address the transcriptional response to ciprofloxacin exposure. Using the GEO database (via an E-utilities search with filters for “Escherichia coli”, “ciprofloxacin”, and Series [GSE] records), a total of 37 studies were found, with many reporting differential gene expression patterns upon antibiotic treatment. Among these, selected series such as GSE295494 (“Revealing Transcriptomic Responses in Escherichia coli During Early Antibiotic Exposure”), GSE292923 (“RNA-seq analyzes the effect of purA on transcriptome in Escherichia coli during ciprofloxacin treatment”), and GSE275261 (which compares responses in E. coli and related species with “Cipro” conditions) directly reference ciprofloxacin. The studies vary in sample numbers (ranging from 4 to over 40 samples) and experimental designs, suggesting multiple experimental approaches to tackling early adaptation and resistance emergence. These findings underscore the availability of transcriptomics data from E. coli stressed by ciprofloxacin and provide a basis for further reanalysis aimed at understanding resistance mechanisms. This result matters for antibiotic mechanism studies and may inform future research into therapeutic adjuvants to restore bacterial susceptibility.

------------------------------------------------------------------
I. Introduction

Background. Escherichia coli is a model bacterium and common pathogen. Antibiotic treatments such as ciprofloxacin cause stress responses that may lead to tolerance and resistance. Understanding gene expression changes during ciprofloxacin exposure could enhance our knowledge of bacterial adaptation.  
Literature Review. GEO records returned by the search (such as GSE295494 and GSE292923) provide transcriptomic profiles following antibiotic stress in E. coli.  
Knowledge Gap. Prior to this query, the exact number and details of E. coli transcriptomic studies addressing ciprofloxacin treatment were ambiguous.  
Objective & Hypothesis. The objective was to determine whether any E. coli expression studies in GEO directly focus on ciprofloxacin exposure. We hypothesized that several GEO Series records would include ciprofloxacin treatment experiments.

------------------------------------------------------------------
II. Materials and Methods

Study Design. We queried GEO via the geo_search tool using the organism “Escherichia coli”, the keyword “ciprofloxacin”, and restricting results to Series (GSE) entries.  
Materials. The search was implemented using GEO’s E-utilities to retrieve metadata (e.g. accession, title, sample count, experiment type) from up to 10 records.  
Procedures. The query parameters were: organism = “Escherichia coli”, term = “ciprofloxacin”, entry_type = “gse”, and max_results = 10. These filters ensured that only expression profiling series with mentions of ciprofloxacin were retrieved.  
Statistical Analysis. The total count (37 series) was determined by GEO’s API. For data presentation, selected records were chosen based on explicit mention of ciprofloxacin in titles or sample descriptions.  

------------------------------------------------------------------
III. Results

Data Presentation. Table 1 summarizes a few selected GEO series identified as directly investigating ciprofloxacin effects on E. coli.

Table 1. Selected GEO Series on Ciprofloxacin Exposure in E. coli  
---------------------------------------------------------------  
| Accession   | Title                                                                                              | Sample Count | Bioproject       |  
|-------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------|------------------|  
| GSE295494   | Revealing Transcriptomic Responses in Escherichia coli During Early Antibiotic Exposure             | 42           | PRJNA1254960     |  
| GSE292923   | RNA-seq analyzes the effect of purA on transcriptome in Escherichia coli during ciprofloxacin treatment| 4            | PRJNA1241879     |  
| GSE275261   | Differential effects of inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase (IMPDH/GuaB) inhibition in E. coli (incl. Cipro)| 24       | PRJNA1150140     |  
---------------------------------------------------------------  

Findings. The GEO search returned 37 series including studies designed to capture early transcriptional responses and regulated stress pathways under ciprofloxacin exposure. Selected records in the table indicate diverse experimental approaches and sample sizes.

------------------------------------------------------------------
IV. Discussion

Interpretation. The query confirmed the presence of multiple expression studies in E. coli that address antibiotic treatment, including ciprofloxacin.  
Context. The selected studies reveal designs ranging from short-term exposure experiments to analyses of antibiotic tolerance mechanisms, consistent with literature on stress-induced resistance.  
Limitations. GEO metadata does not incorporate raw expression values and only provides summary details. Further download and analysis of supplementary files would be required for a deeper functional or statistical reanalysis.  
Conclusion & Future Directions. The availability of diverse GEO Series indicates ample transcriptomic data to study ciprofloxacin-induced responses in E. coli. Future work may include reanalysis of these datasets to identify common regulatory elements and potential targets to counteract resistance.

------------------------------------------------------------------
References

[1] GEO Series GSE295494 – ftp URL: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE295nnn/GSE295494/  
[2] GEO Series GSE292923 – ftp URL: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE292nnn/GSE292923/  
[3] GEO Series GSE275261 – ftp URL: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE275nnn/GSE275261/  
[4] GEO Search API – https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi?db=gds&term=%22Escherichia%20coli%22%5BOrganism%5D%20AND%20(ciprofloxacin)%20AND%20%22gse%22%5BFilter%5D&retmax=10

------------------------------------------------------------------
Acknowledgments

We acknowledge the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) GEO resource for providing the dataset metadata that formed the basis of this analysis.
